message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.85, which filled at $222.85 — about $8,914, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, with only AAPL/MSFT eligible and no money moved out. The business quality in the audited statements supported a buy: revenue of $391.0B (+2% YoY), gross margin of $180.7B (46.2%, up from 44.1%), operating income of $123.2B, operating cash flow of $118.3B, and a Services segment that grew 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin — offset by a one-time $10.2B net EU State Aid tax charge that pushed net income down to $93.7B (diluted EPS $6.08) despite higher operating profit, plus Greater China weakness (−8%) and ongoing DOJ/DMA antitrust exposure. I deliberately discounted the filing's forward-looking claim of ">25% fiscal 2025 net sales growth" and ">40% Services growth" because it contradicts the audited +2% and +13% figures in the same document; on the reliable numbers the shares trade at roughly 36.6x trailing EPS at $222.70, a full but defensible multiple given ~$140.8B of cash and securities and a $110B buyback authorization, which is why I sized this as a modest starter position rather than a full allocation.
